title: A flow sequence left open after an inner one closed, then a line at indentation 0
notes: The flow sequence `[[x], y` is the value of an entry of a block mapping at indentation 0, so it is parsed with n = 1 (productions 187, 192, 194, 196 and 197: the value of an entry at indentation 0 is a flow node at n+1). Every line break inside the flow sequence is crossed by s-separate-lines (production 81) or, inside a plain scalar, s-flow-folded (production 74), and both end with the flow line prefix (production 69): at least one space of indentation. The inner sequence closed, but the outer one is still open when the line break after `y` ends the first line, so the next line must continue it. `z` stands in column 1 with no indentation, so it cannot belong to any valid document; the prefix up to the line break can still be continued by ` ]`. The position is 2:1, the first character of the second line. The input does not end too soon at the break: the character that fails is present, so the end-of-input rule does not apply.

provenance.reference: A reader that forgot the outer open flow sequence once the inner one had closed, and either accepted the next line as a new mapping entry or reported the error at the end of the input instead of at the line that breaks the indentation.
